newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi economy grows by 8.6 pct in 1996 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Saudi economy grows by 8.6 pct in 1996 - minister.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's economy grew by a nominal 8.6 percent in 1996, Saudi Planning Minister Abdul-Wahab bin Abdul-Salam Attar said on Sunday.
The private sector contributed 3.5 percent to the country's gross domestic product (GDP), he added. The current account of the balance of payments also showed the first surplus in 1996 in years.

"This reflects the strength of the Saudi economy in facing local, regional and international changes and dealing with them in a capable manner," Saudi state-run news agency SPA quoted Attar as saying. He gave no further details.
Higher oil prices last year pushed Saudi's revenues some $12 billion over projections and enabled the kingdom to catch up on debt payments.
Its 1997 budget projected a deficit of 17 billion riyals ($4.5 billion) -- steady at the actual 1996 deficit but below the 18.5 billion spending-revenue gap forcast in January 1995.
Bumper oil earnings allowed Riyadh to record a 700 million riyal surplus in the current account of the balance of payments in 1996. Inflation remained subdued at below one percent a year.
Like its oil-rich neighbours, Saudi wants to diversify its economy to reduce vulnerability to fluctuations in world oil prices.
